claims.text: A graph neural network with physics-informed loss functions can predict conductivity in bulk HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than existing analytical approaches.
The proposed model can cover the 0–200 K temperature regime.
The proposed model can cover the 300–1200 K temperature regime.
Accounting for defects will improve conductivity prediction accuracy for bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Accounting for oxygen content will improve conductivity prediction accuracy for bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The samples to which the hypothesis applies are bulk HfNbTaTiZr with and without 1 wt.% oxygen.
The intervention is to train a graph neural network with physics-informed loss functions on experimental data.
Defects and oxygen content are the structural mediators relevant to conductivity prediction.
The graph neural network learns the effects of defects and oxygen content on material properties and thereby predicts conductivity.
Existing analytical calculations can disagree with experimental observations and require further validation.
The proposed model will outperform existing analytical predictions of conductivity for bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The model's accuracy may be limited by the quality and quantity of its training data.
The model should be evaluated against existing analytical predictions on a held-out conductivity dataset.
Conductivity should be measured at multiple temperatures for the held-out benchmark.
Failure to outperform existing analytical predictions on the held-out dataset would falsify the hypothesis.
